Photo geotagging without a track file

No GPX? Use nearby iPhone photos as location clues.

LensPin can use geotagged iPhone photos from the same trip to suggest missing locations for camera photos already in Apple Photos. No GPX recording is required. Check each suggestion before saving; the result depends on the available time and location clues.

Last updated October 21, 2026

How the no-GPX method works

Build a location timeline from photos you already took.

  1. Choose geotagged reference photosUse geotagged iPhone photos or photos from another GPS-equipped camera as reference points.
  2. Compare the nearest timesLensPin looks before and after each adjusted camera capture time.
  3. Check time and distanceNearby reference photos support one another; distant reference photos indicate movement.
  4. Review the suggested pointInspect both reference photos, time gaps, map and explanation before selecting it.

What makes clues stronger

Close in time, close in place, visible on both sides.

Locations agree

Reference photos in the same small area suggest you stayed nearby.

Short time gaps

Minutes are easier to trust than hours; the chosen maximum remains a hard limit.

When the timeline shows movement

LensPin does not draw a straight line between distant photos.

If two reference photos are more than 300 metres apart, LensPin favors the nearer time instead of inventing the route between them. The result is downgraded for review.

Nearby reference photos

Same-area clues

  • Use the shared area as the suggestion
  • Give more weight to short time gaps
Distant reference photos

Movement clues

  • Favor the nearer time with lower confidence
  • Give no suggestion when it is too far away

Only one nearby iPhone photo?

A one-sided clue can help, but it needs more caution.

One close-in-time reference photo can help, but without a second photo it receives a penalty and may land in Review. A 10:02 reference photo can support a 10:07 photo far better than an 11:30 photo.

Matching happens on the device.

Photos are not uploaded, and geotagged photos from iPhone or another GPS-equipped camera can be used as references. Read the privacy details →

Inside the no-GPX review

See what nearby iPhone photos can—and cannot—support.

LensPin keeps both nearby iPhone photos visible so you can tell whether the suggestion represents a stable place, movement, or only a weak one-sided clue.

See the actual reference photos

Before-and-after thumbnails, capture times, time gaps, and map positions stay attached to the camera photo.

Understand movement

Nearby reference photos can support a shared area. Distant reference photos are treated as movement, not as permission to invent a route between them.

Open No Clear Suggestion too

The detail view shows the nearest eligible iPhone photos and which time or distance limit they failed.
